newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa aims to cut costs of drugs, health care.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa aims to cut costs of drugs, health care.

text.p: South Africa plans a thorough overhaul of the pricing and distribution of drugs to reduce costs and increase access to health care, Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma said on Friday.
Addressing a parliamentary media briefing, Zuma said that this would ensure that the prices of drugs in South Africa were comparable to those in the rest of the world.

She denied reports that she planned to prevent doctors from dispensing drugs, but said it was essential that they had dispensing licences in order to eliminate any profit motive for recommending drugs.
At the same time, dispensing pharmacists would be asked to charge a professional fee for their services rather than use profit mark-ups.

Zuma, who upset the tobacco sector by introducing stringent advertising controls and requirements that all tobacco products carry health warnings, said she was now "looking at the next stage" in her dealings with the industry but could not announce anything yet.
She also appealed to the media to launch an awareness campaign on alcohol abuse so that when she took action against alcohol advertisements "the ground will be a bit softer."
Zuma said she would recruit another 363 qualified doctors from other countries this year, mainly Cuba.
